newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Elf, Shell buy Congo refinery's distribution network. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Elf, Shell buy Congo refinery's distribution network. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell NV and Elf Aquitaine SA of France have agreed to jointly buy the distribution network of Hydro-Congo (corrects to make clear they buying the distribution arm not the refinery), the Congolese oil company being sold as part of the state's privatisation programme, for an undisclosed sum, Elf said.
Hydro-Congo has an oil refinery in Congo's economic capital, Pointe Noire, and a network of service stations throughout the country.
The agreement also provides for the companies to manage the refinery in Pointe Noire.
Hydro-Congo has interests in oil exploration, holding permits alongside international operators. It has a 15 percent interest in Nkossa, 35 percent in Kitina and 50 percent in the Yombo permit.

"The agreement was signed at the end of last week at the Congolese embassy in Paris (corrects from "the French Embassy")," a spokesman at Elf's Paris headquarters told Reuters in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo by telephone.
The Anglo-Dutch Shell company and its French counterpart will each take a 50 percent stake in Hydro-Congo.
Three oil companies had been competing to buy Hydro-Congo -- Shell, Elf and The Addax & Oryx Group Ltd of Switzerland.
Congo's capital, Brazzaville, has been battered by fighting since June between the forces of President Pascal Lissouba and allies of his predecessor, Denis Sassou Nguesso.

Asked about the timing of the signature -- on the eve of the latest breach of the ceasefire in Brazzaville and before any conclusion to peace talks -- Elf would only say that the talks had been under way for several months.
"If they've signed at this stage then they're obviously confident the situation will sort itself out," a Congolese government official said.
Hydro-Congo had 1996 sales of between 40 billion and 45 billion CFA francs ($64-$72 million) and a workforce of 1,020.
